title: Scheduled jobs always execute hosts one at a time — no parallel-host option on jobs
existing_state: Interactive runs can batch up to 100 hosts in parallel via the run dialog, but scheduled jobs cannot. Folder jobs build FolderExecutionOptions with only RunPresetsInParallel and StopOnFirstError (Services/JobExecutionService.cs:737-742); ParallelHostCount is never set so it stays at its default of 1 (Models/FolderExecutionOptions.cs:27), which the engine clamps into one-host-at-a-time batches (SshExecutionService.cs:636, 684-691). Single-preset jobs route through ExecutePresetAsync (JobExecutionService.cs:687) whose host loop is strictly sequential by construction (SshExecutionService.cs:434-451, script path 584-597). JobDefinition carries FolderExecutionMode and StopOnError (Models/JobDefinition.cs:229-235) but has no parallelism field, and JobEditorDialog therefore offers none. A nightly job against 200 devices at ~10s each runs 30+ minutes when it could finish in ~2.
recommendation: Add ParallelHostCount to JobDefinition (default 1 for backward compatibility), surface it in JobEditorDialog next to the existing Stop-on-error option, and pass it into FolderExecutionOptions in ExecuteFolderJobAsync. For single-preset jobs, either route them through ExecuteFolderAsync with a one-entry preset dictionary (inherits batching, progress, and stop-on-first-error for free) or add the same batching to ExecuteAsync/ExecuteScriptAsync.
user_benefit: Scheduled fleet jobs finish in minutes instead of hours, and the scheduler reaches feature parity with what the user can already do interactively — important since unattended runs are exactly where long sequential walls hurt most (maintenance windows).

evidence.note: Preset jobs use ExecutePresetAsync — sequential host loop
Job model has FolderExecutionMode + StopOnError but no parallel-host knob
ExecuteAsync/ExecuteScriptAsync iterate hosts strictly sequentially; only ExecuteFolderAsync batches, gated on ParallelHostCount
